audit.whatIsWrong: The First item row said Camille in both layers while whys[5] said 'First item is even', and the packet chart has Skill on that row.
audit.why: Purgatory's grounding is what makes that row even — it removes Hookshot and the Ultimatum dash at once. The prose already knew this; only the chart tokens disagreed.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and win[5] flipped to Skill as a matched pair, rating raised to 5/10. HARD 7/10 overall is kept — 46.92% over 699 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown anchored the 'wait for Hookshot' advice, and the level 6 spike framed Purgatory as trading evenly with her ultimate.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5s, The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90s against Purgatory's 120/100/80s. Purgatory is up more often than her ultimate from rank 1.
audit.corrected: 16s Hookshot stated in mid; the level 6 and first-item text now describes denial rather than a trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep was called true damage; the passive shield was never mentioned; Purgatory was described as trading a totem for her ultimate; ability names were wrong (Ritual Nails, Silver Stake, 'Hextech Ultimatum' without the article).
audit.why: Riot's W text is damage, with the outer half slowing, dealing extra damage AND healing Camille — the trueDamage flag sits on Q, not W. Her passive shields a percentage of max health against the damage type that hit her, so it blunts Locke's magic every time she autos him. Purgatory grounds: a grounded Camille has neither Hookshot nor the Ultimatum dash, which is denial, not a trade. Her R is The Hextech Ultimatum.
audit.corrected: W restated as a slow-and-heal sweet spot (Grievous Wounds live); passive shield stated; Purgatory stated as grounding denial; Soul Nails used and the unnamed passive described by effect.

notes: Packet flagged 'Hextech Ultimatum' as a near-miss name — the correct form is The Hextech Ultimatum, fixed in spikes[1]. wants.foe[2] and wants.you[2] in the full layer still use the short form.
